cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
steps: Open the Cloudflare dashboard and pick the domain {{domain}}.
Go to DNS › Records and click Import and Export › Import DNS records.
Upload the file from "Export zone" here.
Important: set MX and SRV records to DNS only (grey cloud) — mail must not go through Cloudflare's proxy.
Come back here and hit "Check now".

route53.name: Amazon Route 53
steps: Open the Route 53 console and the hosted zone for {{domain}}.
With the AWS CLI: export the zone here and import it with cli53 import.
In the console, create each record with Create record (type, name and value are in the table below).
Leave the TTL at the default (300 s is fine).
Come back here and hit "Check now".

godaddy.name: GoDaddy
steps: Go to My Products › DNS for {{domain}}.
For each row in the table below, click Add and pick the type (MX, TXT, CNAME, SRV).
In Host, enter only the part before the domain — GoDaddy appends {{domain}} for you. Use @ for the root.
For MX, the number before the host is the priority; it goes in the Priority field.
Save and come back for "Check now".

namecheap.name: Namecheap
steps: Go to Domain List › Manage › Advanced DNS for {{domain}}.
Use Add New Record for each row in the table below.
In Host, use @ for the root; Namecheap appends the domain to the rest.
MX records live under Mail Settings, with the Custom MX option.
Save and come back for "Check now".

google.name: Google Domains / Squarespace
steps: Open the DNS settings for {{domain}}.
Under Custom records, create one entry per row in the table below.
Use @ for the root; the rest of the host goes without the trailing domain.
Save and come back for "Check now".

other.name: Another provider
steps: Find the DNS, Zone editor or Records section in the control panel.
Create one entry per row in the table below, with the same type, host and value.
If the panel appends the domain to the host itself, drop the trailing ".{{domain}}"; use @ for the root.
If it accepts a zone file import, use "Export zone" — faster and no typos.
Come back here and hit "Check now".

migration.title: Import mail
migration.blurb: Copies the folders and messages from your previous provider into this mailbox. The old account is left exactly as it is, and nothing is deleted there.
migration.hostHint: The IMAP server address. For Google it is imap.gmail.com, for Microsoft 365 it is outlook.office365.com.
migration.passwordHint: With two-step verification enabled, Google and Microsoft require an application-specific password rather than the account password.
migration.cancelKeeps: Stopping keeps every message already copied. Nothing is removed from this mailbox or from the previous provider.

skip.virtual: The provider presents this as a folder, but its messages are already in the folders above. Copying it would duplicate every message in the account.

migration.providerHint: Outlook and Thunderbird are mail programs, not providers. Select the provider the account belongs to, or choose another IMAP server and enter the address the program was set up with.

notice.appPassword: With two-step verification enabled, this provider requires an application-specific password rather than the account password.
notice.oauthOnly: Microsoft has withdrawn password authentication for IMAP. An import from Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com requires OAuth, which is not yet available here.

migration.promptBody: The mail held by a previous provider can be copied into this mailbox, with the folder tree, the received dates and the read state intact.
migration.promptSafety: Nothing is removed from the previous account. The import can also be started later, from your account.
migration.fileBlurb: For mail that is on no server: messages downloaded by POP3 years ago, an archive exported before an account was closed, or a mailbox handed over when somebody left.
migration.fileDrop: Drop the file here, or select it
migration.fileFormats: Accepted: Thunderbird mailbox files (Local Folders, with or without a .mbox extension), .eml messages, and a .zip containing either. Up to 500 MB per upload — larger mailboxes can be sent one folder at a time.
migration.whereThunderbird: Settings → General → Config Editor is not needed. Use Help → Troubleshooting Information → Profile Folder → Open Folder, then the Mail directory. Each mailbox is the file without an extension; the .msf beside it is only an index. Compressing the Mail folder into a .zip and uploading that brings the whole tree at once.
migration.whereOutlook: Outlook stores mail in a .pst file, which is a database rather than mail and cannot be read here. Add this mailbox to Outlook as an ordinary account, then drag the folders from the .pst onto it: Outlook uploads the messages itself, and the result is more faithful than any conversion.
migration.fileTooLargeLocal: That file is {{size}}, above the 500 MB limit for one upload. Send the folders separately, or compress a smaller part of the tree.
